title: Publish snapshots with an explicit "as of" banner instead of pretending to be live
problem_it_solves: The sandbox cannot reach nfl.com from CI, so an unattended hourly refresh is not possible today; readers could mistake a snapshot for live data
proposal: Ship each data table with a fetched-at timestamp, the source URL, and a staleness badge that turns amber past the budget and red past 24h; treat refresh as a deliberate operation, not a background promise
evidence: Implemented in this build as the first step; the timestamp is rendered from the CSV metadata
recommended_path: Adopt as-is; add a scheduled workflow later if egress is granted

title: Make "not published" a first-class value in the data layer
problem_it_solves: The requirement "leave it blank and flag it" needs a mechanical representation, otherwise blanks silently become zeros
proposal: Store empty strings for unknowns, never 0 or "N/A"; the builder renders the literal phrase not published and the audit counts them
evidence: verify.py enforces it: a blank with no matching flag fails the build
recommended_path: Keep; extend the rule to numeric fields (already enforced)

title: Gate the leaderboard on data readiness, not on results
problem_it_solves: A leaderboard with zero tracked bets invites fake rankings; but a competition without any visible state is not reviewable
proposal: Rank nothing yet. Publish a Gate Readiness board: each strategy is shown with which gates it can even be evaluated on, and what blocks the rest
evidence: Implemented: pages/leaderboard.html renders readiness, not performance
recommended_path: Keep until the first forward-tracked bet settles, then switch to results + gates together

title: Pre-register every strategy; forbid backtest numbers from ever appearing on the leaderboard
problem_it_solves: Retrospective results are the single largest source of self-deception in this kind of project
proposal: Require a hash-stamped spec (inputs, markets, rules, gate set, planned sample) before any tracking starts; forward-only results; backtests live on a separate, clearly labelled research page
evidence: No evidence needed beyond arithmetic; the failure mode is documented in the correlation/parlay literature as a matching artefact (S-PITH-PARLAY)
recommended_path: Adopt; it is the cheapest large win available

title: Limit v1 scope to straight bets and single-player game props
problem_it_solves: Sixteen gates × six bet types cannot be built at once, and half of them have no data source yet
proposal: v1 = spread, total, ML + a prop layer for rush/reception yards and passes; defer live betting, futures, team totals, alternate lines
evidence: Requirement R-12/R-13/R-14 all satisfied by that subset
recommended_path: Adopt, or explicitly choose the wider scope and accept a longer gate build

title: Build the availability graph as a first-class dataset (who was expected to start, who actually did)
problem_it_solves: The brief's core requirement — backups replacing starters — cannot be answered from the injury hub alone, and there is no official depth chart
proposal: Model each club-week as: roster status (ACT/IR/PUP/NFI/PS) → practice participation → designation → projected starter → actual starter → snap share; store every state as a dated event so we can reconstruct what was knowable when
evidence: Our Week 10 ingest already proves three of the five stages; the projected-starter and snap stages are the gap
recommended_path: Adopt as the next build item; it is the project's actual differentiator

title: Do not model depth from jersey order; model it from playing time
problem_it_solves: Depth-chart rank is unavailable; guessing 2nd-string from a roster list would be inference, which the brief forbids
proposal: Quantify replacement cost with the gap between the last two games' production of the departing starter and the production of whoever actually filled the snaps, using only data we are entitled to store
evidence: Official practice participation is a weak proxy; snap data is not yet licensed
recommended_path: Adopt only when Q-02 closes; until then publish the deficiency table with blank effect columns

title: Set the promotion sample at n>=400 bets with a +CLV floor, and a 1,000-bet tier for real staking
problem_it_solves: Is this skill or luck? needs a number, not a vibe
proposal: Gate G-08 = 400 settled, G-09 = 1,000 settled for tier promotion, both requiring the mean CLV to be positive with a two-sided 95% interval that excludes zero
evidence: R-17; the sample-size arithmetic is computed on the Skill vs Luck page from the published formulas
recommended_path: Adopt; the numbers are a policy choice but the derivation is shown so they can be argued with

title: Define the benchmark close as the median of at least three independent prices, and record dispersion
problem_it_solves: A single book's close is both noisy and manipulable, and CLV against it is not a clean skill signal
proposal: Consensus close = median across a fixed book panel; store interquartile range; reject the price if fewer than three quotes exist
evidence: Standard market-construction practice
recommended_path: Adopt with Q-01

title: Score parlays on the independence baseline, but settle them on the true joint
problem_it_solves: Parlays are where operators earn their margin; a naive model that multiplies independent leg probabilities systematically overstates parlay value
proposal: Publish both: the independence-implied price and the correlation-adjusted price; the gate is on the difference between our joint estimate and the offered price
evidence: Independent research on cross-game parlays finds prices drifting above the product of their own legs' prices, growing with leg count, while a public review disputes the matching method — so the direction is plausible and the magnitude is not established
recommended_path: Adopt the framework; explicitly mark every magnitude as unverified until we fit our own

title: Treat same-game prop combos as a volume-conservation problem, not a correlation-coefficient problem
problem_it_solves: A correlation matrix across 400 props is un-estimable at our data volume
proposal: Model the constraint instead: team pass/rush volume is a finite budget, so two teammates' receptions are negatively coupled by construction and a stack with the QB is positively coupled by construction; only game-score coupling stays positive
evidence: Derived reasoning; no external claim needed
recommended_path: Adopt; it gives a structural prior that does not require fitting a huge matrix

title: Make the injury signal a *surprise*, never a level
problem_it_solves: Public knowledge of an injury is already priced; only the delta moves value
proposal: Signal = (expected availability from the prior day's trend) − (realized designation/participation); trade only when surprise exceeds the noise floor
evidence: The Week 10 data shows the mechanism exists: SEA's hub page reported nothing while the same site reported Darnold out — a real information-timing gap
recommended_path: Adopt; this is the highest-conviction signal family we can build from the data we already hold

title: Freeze the verification vocabulary: verified / corroborated / unverified — and never let marketing copy widen it
problem_it_solves: Overstating verification is the fastest way to make a dataset unusable
proposal: verified = transcribed from an official league page with a recomputation check; corroborated = two independent official pages agree; unverified = anything else, rendered with a flag link
evidence: Implemented: verify.py enforces it at build time
recommended_path: Adopt and keep; add the sign-off box (see Q-28)

title: Obtain the league's own injury-reporting policy text and store it in-repo with a hash
problem_it_solves: Timing rules (when a club must file, what DNP/Limited/Full oblige them to disclose) are currently only documented by third parties, which the brief disallows as a system of record
proposal: Fetch the official operations policy page, save the text and the URL, and cite the local copy everywhere the rule is used
evidence: Confirmed negative result: operations.nfl.com's landing page does not expose a fetchable rule page at the paths we tried (FLAG-05)
recommended_path: Adopt; until it closes, all timing-based signals stay gated

title: Run the 32-team roster/IR sweep before any team-level model is trusted
problem_it_solves: A surprise-heavy roster year (Garrett on LAR, Parsons on GB, Evans on SF) is exactly where a silent join failure becomes a silent model error
proposal: Nightly sweep of all 32 roster pages; diff to the previous day; alert on any player whose team in the injury report does not appear in that team's roster list
evidence: Spot-check on one club (NE) succeeded and produced usable status codes
recommended_path: Adopt as a prerequisite for gate G-02

title: Add a fixture-context feature set built only from published schedule facts
problem_it_solves: Rest days, travel, timezone offset, altitude, dome/open and short weeks are verifiable and cheap, unlike most "situational" folklore
proposal: Derive rest delta from official kickoff timestamps; travel flag from venue cities; short-week flag when a club plays Thursday after Sunday
evidence: Week 10 contains two real cases: the Munich 09:30 ET game and a Monday game for a club coming off a Thursday game
recommended_path: Adopt; keep the priors at zero until measured, so the feature cannot smuggle in a belief

title: Store every model output as a probability plus its inputs, not just a pick
problem_it_solves: A pick without its inputs cannot be debugged, attributed, or reproduced after a data change
proposal: Immutable prediction log keyed by (game, market, timestamp) holding our fair value, the benchmark price, the inputs hash and the gate set version
evidence: No external evidence needed; this is what makes the leaderboard auditable
recommended_path: Adopt before any strategy is tracked

title: Compute and publish the "removal of luck" panel on the site dashboard
problem_it_solves: The brief asks to remove luck; that is only credible if the reader sees it every week
proposal: Weekly panel: bets placed, mean CLV with interval, bootstrap p-value on ROI, split-half agreement, and a "luck-adjusted" PnL (results re-priced at fair odds)
evidence: Formulas already derived on the Skill vs Luck page
recommended_path: Adopt; renders "insufficient sample" until the sample exists

title: Do not accept the label "No Injuries Reported" as a zero
problem_it_solves: If a club's row set is missing, a coverage-weighted model treats it as a healthy team and prices the opponent's pass catchers too cheaply
proposal: Distinguish "empty because reported" from "empty because not fetched/not published" and refuse to treat the second as data
evidence: Directly observed in the Week 10 pull: SEA empty, PIT's opponents CIN empty, LAC and BAL empty on a Monday night
recommended_path: Adopt; the builder already renders these as not published

title: Separate the site's "findings" from its "specifications" visually and permanently
problem_it_solves: A dashboard that mixes measured facts with design intentions invites decisions made on intentions
proposal: Two persistent page families, tinted differently: everything measured comes from data/*.csv; everything specified is prose with a status chip; no page mixes both without a divider
evidence: Implemented as a per-page type badge in the header
recommended_path: Keep; consider a legend on the landing page

title: Add a two-sided "what would change our mind" field to every strategy entry
problem_it_solves: A leaderboard without falsification criteria turns into a belief-confirmation machine
proposal: Require each strategy to declare, at registration, the observation that would kill it (e.g. "CLV interval crosses zero at n=400", "hit rate on Q4 is within 2 pts of the book's")
evidence: Design convention
recommended_path: Adopt; cheap and it improves the review conversation

title: Price a line ourselves and publish the residual against the market, on a schedule, from day one
problem_it_solves: Originating lines only becomes real once we can show our number, not just our method
proposal: Weekly "origination card": for each game, our model number (blank until the model exists), the market consensus (blank until licensed), the residual (blank), and the gate that is currently blocking each column
evidence: Nothing in-repo yet — the whole point is to expose the blanks
recommended_path: Adopt as the site's spine; the blanks are the honest state of the project

title: Version the data dictionary with the site, and make schema drift a build failure
problem_it_solves: Tables rebuilt by several sessions drift; a renamed column silently breaks every downstream model
proposal: Migrate data/*.csv headers to a checked-in schema file; the audit fails when a CSV and the schema disagree
evidence: The pipe-delimited CSVs already have a header row that the generator depends on
recommended_path: Adopt in the integration pass

title: Keep the leaderboard free of any number we cannot source, including our own estimates
problem_it_solves: A single plausible-looking placeholder in a table becomes a citable "fact" within a week
proposal: Audit rule: any numeric cell whose source is not an official row fails the build; only arithmetic we performed in-repo may be numeric, and it must link to the formula
evidence: Implemented in verify.py; the correlation and strategy tables are consequently almost entirely blank
recommended_path: Keep — the blanks are the deliverable

title: Decide the reward mechanism before publishing a competition
problem_it_solves: A competition without a real prize produces strategy theatre: many entries, no accountability
proposal: Choose one: (a) staking allocation only, (b) compute/data budget, (c) real bankroll share with clawback; publish the payout formula next to the tier table
risk: Medium — it is a money decision
evidence: Tier design is complete and deliberately leaves the payout formula unfunded
recommended_path: Owner decision; default to (a) until a bankroll exists

title: Turn the 136-game log into the pre-registered backtest corpus
problem_it_solves: Every strategy is currently untestable: the minimum-sample gate and the pre-registration rule have nothing to run against because this session had no historical results file. The merged week 1-9 log is that file, and it now reconciles with the independently transcribed standings table.
proposal: Wire data/games_2026_wk1_9.csv into the strategy harness as the only permitted backtest window (weeks 1-9); record the file's SHA-256 inside each strategy's registration entry so a later edit to the corpus invalidates the grade; publish every grade with its fold boundaries and its settled-leg count; keep grades off the leaderboard per S-04.
risk: Medium-high. Nine weeks is a small historical window and 16 of 32 clubs have a bye inside it, so week-over-week comparisons are unbalanced; over-fitting is the default outcome unless the pre-registration discipline in S-04 is enforced by the harness rather than by prose.
evidence: The log is 136 rows, each with an official nfl.com game URL, and the recount matches the standings table for 32 of 32 clubs (tools/verify.py, recomputed on every build).
recommended_path: Register the corpus hash in tools/, then run exactly one strategy end to end and publish its grade with the settled-leg count beside it. Do not back-fill grades for strategies registered before the corpus existed.

title: Choose one canonical site layout and label the other three
problem_it_solves: Four HTML trees are published at once: this audited dashboard at the root, session arena-01b698ef's register dashboard under review/, and two builds of session arena-009ec582's site under archive/session-009ec582/ and docs/. A reader arriving from the live URL cannot tell which register is authoritative, a future session can edit the wrong tree, and the collision has already forced one tool rename (FL-19).
proposal: Keep the root as the only build this CI audits. Add one banner line to review/index.html and docs/index.html naming the root dashboard as current and linking to it (the archived copy already carries one), and state in README which paths are frozen. Do not delete any archived tree until its tables have been absorbed and re-audited here.
risk: Low for the banner. Deleting the archived build would destroy the only rendering of that session's team-stat and player-leader work, which has not been re-derived here.
evidence: All four trees are in the merged commit; the archived pages render standalone because their stylesheet and script were copied beside them, and each tree is checked by a different workflow (validate.yml for the root, verify.yml for review/).
recommended_path: Add the banner in the next change to review/index.html and docs/index.html (owned by those sessions' scopes), and open a task to absorb their team-stat and register tables into the audited site before any deletion is considered.

title: Publish a canonical club-key registry and force every join through it
problem_it_solves: FL-17 is the first join bug of this class and it was silent: 31 of 32 clubs reconciled between two official tables and one simply looked absent, because the standings page codes the Rams LAR and the schedule pages code them LA. Prices, injury reports, rosters and standings each use their own abbreviations and slugs.
proposal: Add data/teams.csv as the single key source: canonical id, official name, and the code used by each upstream surface (standings, schedule and game pages, injury hub, roster pages, and the odds feed once one exists). The builder and verify.py then refuse to join any table whose club key is not registered, and an unregistered key fails the build instead of dropping rows.
risk: Low mechanically, but it touches every data file and the builder's join path, so it must land with the auditors updated in the same commit or the site will fail to build.
evidence: Two separate key hazards are already flagged (FL-15 player slug versus display name, FL-17 club code), and both were found by arithmetic rather than by reading.
recommended_path: Create the registry now, before odds data or a second season arrives; convert the four published tables to join through it; keep the raw upstream code in each row so a reader can still check the source page.

title: Decide the price-data policy before any backtest is published
problem_it_solves: Three quarters of this project's blocked features - vig removal, CLV as the skill measure, closing-line validation of model prices, and every gate that needs a market benchmark - are blocked on one input, and the repository now contains a third-party historical set that looks like it solves the problem but does not: its closing lines stop in 2018 and its 2026 prices are a timestamp-free single field covering 163 of 272 games (FL-21).
proposal: Choose one of three paths and write it into the rules: (a) license or build a market feed with capture timestamps, book identity and revision history, which is the only route to a publishable CLV figure; (b) declare the project model-price-only, publish fair values with no market comparison at all, and delete the temptation by moving third-party lines to an offline research directory excluded from the site build; or (c) use the 2006-2018 historical set strictly as an offline backtest exhibit, clearly outside the audited site, to develop the harness without pretending it prices a 2026 game.
risk: High if left undecided: the most likely failure mode of this project is a future session quietly computing vig from a moneyline column and publishing it as if it were a market statement.
evidence: Measured in the merged tree: closing_lines.csv = 20,490 rows / seasons 2006-2018 / 0 rows in 2026; games.csv 2026 = 272 rows with 163 non-empty moneyline cells; upstream leesharpe/nfldata publishes no LICENSE (their own provenance note).
recommended_path: Decide (b) or (c) now and (a) only with a budget: (b) keeps the site honest with zero spend, and it is the option this session would pick. Whichever is chosen, the rule must be enforced by tools/verify.py refusing any published cell that cites a price file - the enforcement is the point, not the prose.

title: Automate a nightly official-source diff so coverage drift is caught by code, not by a session
problem_it_solves: Eight audit suites passed while the published site claimed a 28-club snapshot that held 24, and while two clubs with full injury blocks sat absent. The audits compare the site to data/; nothing compared data/ to the league, so a one-off manual re-fetch was the only thing that found it (FL-24).
proposal: Add a scheduled workflow that re-fetches the official standings, schedule and injury hub, and failing-closed compares them to data/. It should not auto-overwrite the site: it should open an issue or fail a check naming exactly which rows changed. Standings and fixtures are cheap and stable enough to diff every day; the injury hub changes three times a week, which is precisely why it needs a scheduled snapshot.
risk: Low - it only reads official pages and writes a report
evidence: This session: 32/32 standings rows and 14/14 fixtures matched live pages exactly, so a diff on those is low-noise. Injury coverage did not match, and a diff would have caught it the day it appeared.
recommended_path: recommended

title: Derive every published count from the file it describes, and fail the build on any prose number
problem_it_solves: The same class of defect appeared four times: prose said `28 clubs`, `25 suggestions`, `28 questions` and `15 flags` against files holding 24, 29, 29 and 22. Each was individually correct when written and silently aged as other sessions appended rows.
proposal: Extend the guard added this session beyond the registers. Any "N <noun>" in content/*.md where <noun> maps to a data file should be replaced by a generated metric reference or checked at build time. The rule to state in the methodology: no prose number that a file can be asked about.
evidence: tools/verify.py gained register_counts_match_files() this session and immediately found one more stale count (R-25). The class is real and recurs.
recommended_path: recommended

title: Publish a coverage scorecard: which clubs, positions and filings are present, per page
problem_it_solves: Coverage gaps were invisible. A reader of the injury page could not tell that two of the 28 playing clubs were missing without counting rows. The depth page covers 4 of 32 clubs and said so only in prose.
proposal: Put a small, generated coverage block at the top of every measured page: clubs expected (from the fixture list) vs clubs present, rows expected vs present where an expectation exists, and the date of the snapshot. It is arithmetic over files already in the repo and needs no new source.
evidence: injury_coverage_is_measured_not_named() now computes 24 of 28 automatically; the same pattern generalises to every measured page.
recommended_path: recommended

title: Build the 32-club depth transcription as the next data task, because it is the only route to R-20/R-21
problem_it_solves: The site can now answer "who is playing instead" for 4 clubs and 17 position groups, including 3 cases down to a third string. The requirement asks for the whole league, and 28 clubs still have no verified chart.
proposal: Transcribe all 32 club charts one position group at a time, recording the club URL and the chart date for each. Validate every chart against that club's own roster page so a stale chart cannot enter silently. Extend computed_depth_reach.csv and the reproducibility check will hold it honest automatically.
risk: Low - additive data, existing verifier already recomputes the join
evidence: This session demonstrated the join works and produces defensible cases on 4 clubs (NE RB to a 3rd string, GB LG and GB LB likewise), so the method is proven and only the transcription remains.
recommended_path: recommended

title: Treat the points-only baseline's measured bias as a benchmark to beat, not a parameter to tune
problem_it_solves: The first originated lines show two embarrassing but useful properties: mean fair total 48.64 against a 45.93 sample mean (biased high by 2.7), and a maximum spread of 7.69 where markets quote 10-plus. Both come from the same cause - no opponent adjustment and no injury weighting.
proposal: Freeze these numbers as the published baseline v0 and require every future model to report against them. Then add, in order: opponent-adjusted ratings, then the availability weighting from the depth work, publishing the change in mean total and spread dispersion each time. A model that cannot be shown to beat v0 should not replace it.
risk: Low - the baseline is already computed and reproducible
evidence: computed_fair_lines.csv, recomputed and re-verified on every build; the bias figures are arithmetic on 136 verified games.
recommended_path: recommended
